title: fix(app-shell): the bell's Activity rows name their object by its label, not its API name (objectui#12212)
body:
Fixes #12212

Clause-②: no

## What changed

The bell's Activity tab (`InboxPopover`) printed each row's object by its API name (`… · sys_user_preference`, `… · crm_lead`) beside a summary that already names the object by its label. The row's second line now shows the object's label in the reader's language, and the API name only when nothing names the object. `sys_activity` still stores `object_name`, and the console resolves it, as triage `6121938464` directs.

- `packages/app-shell/src/layout/InboxPopover.tsx`: a module-private `ActivityObjectLabel` component renders the object half of the row's second line. It finds the definition in `useMetadata().objects` (`findByName`), reads its `label` in the active language (`metadataText`, which also reads an inline locale map), and passes that through `useObjectLabel().objectLabel`, so a bundle entry `objects.NAME.label` wins, as on the console's other object surfaces. An empty answer falls back to the API name. These are the three readers `useNavTargetLabel` composes for an object, imported from that module, not copied.
- New pin: `packages/app-shell/src/layout/__tests__/InboxPopover.activityObjectLabel-12212.test.tsx`.
- `.changeset/12212-activity-object-label.md` (`@object-ui/app-shell` patch).

No new i18n key, no export, prop or type change, nothing on the server. `activityItemType.ts` is read, not changed: the lookup needs the reader's language and the cached definitions, both React context, so it sits at the render, not in the row mapping that Home's card shares.

## Where the definitions come from (H1)

`useMetadata().objects`: `MetadataProvider`'s per-type cache of the `object` list, the same list `useNavTargetLabel`, `useRecentItemLabel` and the app sidebar read. It is one list request for the whole type, shared with every other reader, never one per row (no N requests for N rows). The `object` type is not eager (`EAGER_TYPES` is `app` and `view`), and reading `objects` is what loads it. So the lookup is its own component: the row elements are built on every render of the bell, open or closed, and only a mounted row reads the list. The pin's last case holds both halves: a closed bell reads the list zero times, and the Activity tab with rows reads it.

## Objects the console has not loaded (H2)

Read at objectstack `origin/main` `794177d9b`, in `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts`: the `object` list answer (`createMetaListAnswer`) prunes each object's `listViews` per caller (`createMetaListReadGate`, `filterObjectListViewsForUser`) and masks fields (`maskMetaObjectList`). It drops no object. So a system object such as `sys_user_preference` is in the list the console caches, with its `label`, which the list's translation step serves in the request locale. Two cases can still miss: the list has not loaded yet (the row shows the API name until it lands, then re-renders with the label), or the object has since been removed. Both fall back to the API name, per the ruling. This is a reading of the source, not a live call.

## Translation (H3) and the summary (H4)

`objectLabel` tries `objects.NAME.label` under every app namespace the loaded bundle carries (and the un-prefixed base name), falling back to the definition's label. The pin's `zh-CN` case reads `线索` from a bundle entry for `crm_lead`. The summary (`description`) is server text and is rendered unchanged; the pin asserts it verbatim in `en` and `zh-CN`.

## Tests

Every run below is on `9662600`, this branch's head when the PR was opened.

- New pin, 6 cases: `en` business object shows `Lead`; `en` system object shows `User Preference` (the staging row); `zh-CN` shows `线索` from the bundle; an unknown object shows `crm_gone`; the summaries are verbatim in both languages; a closed bell reads no object list, and the Activity rows read it. Result: 6 passed.
- Ablation 1, the row put back on the API name (through objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`; mutation and restore proven by blob hash, `git diff HEAD` empty after): `4 failed | 2 passed`. The three label cases and the read case are red; the fallback and the summary are green, as the pin's header predicted before the run.
- Ablation 2, the component boundary removed (`ActivityObjectLabel` called as a function inside the row map): `1 failed | 5 passed`, failing with `read while the bell is closed: expected 3 to be +0`. The laziness claim in the code comment is measured.
- Targeted vitest, every test naming `InboxPopover`, `activityItemType` or `inbox-activity`: 28 files, 290 tests passed. Every test naming `AppHeader`, `ConsoleLayout` or `InboxPopover` (the bell's hosts, several with a mocked `useObjectLabel`): 82 files, 719 tests passed.
- `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...' --concurrency=2`: 28 of 28 tasks. `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (both `tsc` legs): exit 0, and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` includes the new pin.
- Gates, each exit 0: `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check-changeset-presence.mjs`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:phantom-deps`, `check:esm-specifiers`, `check:self-import`, `check:i18n-keys`, `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, `check-changeset-fixed.mjs`, `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs`.
- ESLint, narrowed to the 2 touched `.tsx` files: the config's TS block is `files: ['**/*.{ts,tsx}']` and neither path is ignored; `--format json` reports 2 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings. Invariance: the config sets no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService` (no type-aware linting), and no rule under `eslint-rules/` reads the filesystem, so this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file. The full `pnpm lint` is CI's.

## Acceptance notes

- The same defect on a second surface, outside this claim's file surface and not touched here: Home's activity card, `HomeActivity` in `packages/app-shell/src/console/home/HomeRail.tsx`, renders the same shared feed's rows with the same `timeAgo(...) · a.objectName` line. A throwaway probe (deleted, never committed) rendering `HomeActivity` with a `crm_lead` row and a `crm_lead` definition labelled `Lead` read `"3 hours ago · crm_lead"`. Reported to the seat. Moving `ActivityObjectLabel` to a shared module would serve both surfaces.
